questions.prompt: Which everyday product is made using fermentation by microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Yoghurt is made when bacteria ferment milk sugar (lactose) into lactic acid, thickening and souring the milk.

questions.prompt: In genetic engineering, DNA ligase acts most like:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins (seals) pieces of DNA together, acting like molecular glue, while restriction enzymes do the cutting.

questions.prompt: A plasmid is useful in genetic engineering mainly because it can:
options: Carry a chosen gene into a bacterial cell
questions.explanation: A plasmid is a small DNA ring that acts as a carrier (vector), taking an inserted gene into the bacterial cell so the gene can be copied and used.

questions.prompt: Why must the SAME restriction enzyme be used to cut both the insulin gene and the plasmid?
options: So both pieces have matching ends that can join
questions.explanation: Using the same restriction enzyme produces matching (complementary) cut ends on the gene and plasmid, allowing them to fit together before ligase seals them.

questions.prompt: Which group of microorganisms includes yeasts and moulds?
questions.explanation: Fungi include yeasts and moulds; yeast helps make bread, and some moulds produce the antibiotic penicillin.

questions.prompt: A patient has a bacterial throat infection. Which treatment is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacteria, so a bacterial infection can be treated with an antibiotic; antibiotics do not work on viruses.

questions.prompt: Why is a virus often described as being on the border between living and non-living?
options: It is too small to see
It cannot reproduce without a living host cell
questions.explanation: A virus has no machinery of its own and can only reproduce by taking over a living host cell, so it shows life-like behaviour only inside a host.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the four main microbe groups is CORRECT?
options: Bacteria have a true nucleus enclosing their DNA
Plasmodium, which causes malaria, is a protozoan
All fungi cause disease in humans
questions.explanation: Plasmodium is a protozoan spread by mosquitoes. Bacteria lack a true nucleus, most fungi are harmless or useful, and viruses are the smallest microbes.

questions.prompt: An organism with two identical alleles for a gene (such as TT) is described as:
questions.explanation: Homozygous means having two identical alleles (TT or tt); heterozygous means two different alleles (Tt).

questions.prompt: In a Tt x tt cross (T is tall, dominant), what fraction of offspring are expected to be short?
questions.explanation: Tt x tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers, so half the offspring are tt (short) and half are Tt (tall).

questions.prompt: A recessive trait can appear in a child even though neither parent shows it because the parents:
options: Each carry a hidden recessive allele
Have no alleles for the trait
questions.explanation: Each parent can be heterozygous (carrying one hidden recessive allele); when both pass the recessive allele, the child is homozygous recessive and shows the trait.

questions.prompt: A heterozygous tall plant (Tt) is crossed with a homozygous tall plant (TT). What is the expected phenotype of the offspring?
questions.explanation: TT x Tt gives genotypes TT and Tt only; every offspring has at least one dominant T allele, so all are tall.

questions.prompt: Differences between individuals in a population, such as size or colour, are called:
questions.explanation: Variation refers to the inherited differences between individuals, and it provides the raw material that natural selection acts on.

questions.prompt: Closely related species are expected to share:
questions.explanation: More closely related species share more of their DNA, which is strong molecular evidence that they descended from a recent common ancestor.

questions.prompt: In a population of light and dark moths on dark tree bark, why do dark moths become more common over time?
options: The moths decide to change colour
Dark moths are camouflaged, so more survive and reproduce
Birds prefer to eat dark moths
questions.explanation: Dark moths are better hidden on dark bark, so predators eat fewer of them; the survivors reproduce and pass on the dark allele, making it more common.

questions.prompt: A bird at first flies away from a new scarecrow but after several days ignores it completely. This change shows that the bird has:
options: Lost the ability to see the scarecrow
Learned to ignore a repeated harmless stimulus (habituation)
questions.explanation: The bird still senses the scarecrow but learns it is harmless and ignores it, saving energy; this learned change is called habituation.

questions.prompt: Newly hatched ducklings follow the first moving object they see early in life. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Imprinting is rapid learning during a short sensitive period, in which a young animal attaches to the first moving object, usually its mother.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of a behaviour with its correct type is RIGHT?
options: Pulling your hand off a hot pot - learned behaviour
A spider spinning a web with no teaching - instinct
A trained dog sitting on command - innate behaviour
questions.explanation: Web-spinning is a complex inborn behaviour (instinct). Pulling away from heat is a reflex (innate), and a dog sitting on command is learned by conditioning.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, so they have thick muscular walls; veins return blood to the heart.

questions.prompt: Exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste between blood and body cells happens mainly in the:
questions.explanation: Capillaries have very thin walls and a huge surface area, allowing substances to diffuse quickly between blood and cells.

questions.prompt: The left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle because it must:
options: Pump blood only to the nearby lungs
Pump blood at high pressure all around the body
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood through the whole body (systemic circulation), needing more force, while the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.

questions.prompt: If all the producers were removed from an ecosystem, what would happen first to the consumers?
options: They would increase because of less competition
They would lose their energy source and begin to die off
Nothing, because consumers make their own food
questions.explanation: Producers capture the energy that enters the food chain; without them, consumers have no food source and the whole chain collapses from the bottom up.

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass to grasshopper to bird to hawk, why are there far fewer hawks than blades of grass?
options: Only about 10% of energy passes to each next level
questions.explanation: About 90% of energy is lost as heat and used for life processes at each step, so only around 10% passes on, supporting fewer organisms at higher levels.

questions.prompt: Protecting a species by keeping it safe in a national park in its natural habitat is an example of:
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat, for example within national parks such as the Simien Mountains National Park.
